title: 3rd Stopping Place 2nd Truth From The Comprehensiveness Of Mercifulness To Unity And Oneness

questions.question: In the comparison with the sun, what does the sun’s light help explain?
questions.answer: It helps explain how one reality can reach everything and show that its source is one.

questions.question: How do bright and clear objects in that example point to the sun’s oneness?
questions.answer: They each reflect its light, warmth, and colors, showing that the same sun is shining on all of them.

questions.question: What conclusion does a person reach after seeing sunlight spread everywhere it can reach?
questions.answer: He understands that the sun is single and unique.

questions.question: What does the reflection of the sun in many objects suggest about nearness?
questions.answer: It suggests that the sun’s effects appear close to all those things through their reflections.

questions.question: In the passage, what does all-encompassing mercy show about the Merciful One?
questions.answer: It shows His unity and that He has no partner.

questions.question: Besides mercy itself, what else is said to appear in created things, especially living beings and human beings?
questions.answer: Signs of many Divine Names and a kind of manifestation connected to His essence appear in them.

questions.question: What special quality does life give to an individual according to the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a broad connection that makes the individual related to the whole universe.

questions.question: How does that broad connection support the idea of oneness?
questions.answer: It shows that the One who gives life works in all things and is present with all things.

questions.question: What does the passage say is gathered into each living member of animal species, especially in man?
questions.answer: Samples of many Divine gifts and blessings are brought together in each one.

questions.question: How is the care given to each individual described?
questions.answer: It is described as special and personal care, while the order of the whole universe still remains intact.

questions.question: Why is man given a special place in this discussion?
questions.answer: Because many kinds of Divine bounty are displayed in him in a concentrated way.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of the melon and its seed?
questions.answer: The one who makes the full thing must also be the one who makes its concentrated form.

questions.question: Why would it be impossible for another maker to produce the seed in that example?
questions.answer: Because the seed is drawn from the melon with precise knowledge, balance, and wisdom that belong to the same maker.

questions.question: In the final comparison, what are the cosmos, the earth, and man likened to?
questions.answer: The cosmos is like a tree or garden, the earth like a fruit or melon, and man like a seed.

questions.question: Based on that comparison, what must be true about the Creator of the smallest living thing?
questions.answer: That Creator must also be the Creator of the earth and the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What main religious truth is being argued through the example of sunlight and mercy?
questions.answer: The passage argues for Divine oneness and unity.

questions.question: Why is sunlight used as a useful comparison here?
questions.answer: Because one sun reaches many things at once, so it helps the reader imagine how one source can be connected to all.

questions.question: What features of the sun are seen reflected in shining objects?
questions.answer: Its light, heat, and colors are reflected.

questions.question: What does the spread of those reflections reveal about the sun itself?
questions.answer: It reveals that one sun is behind all those reflections.

questions.question: How is Divine mercy similar to the light in the comparison?
questions.answer: It surrounds and reaches everything in a wide and inclusive way.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does this universal mercy rule out?
questions.answer: It rules out the idea that the Merciful One has any partner.

questions.question: Where are the signs of many Divine Names especially seen?
questions.answer: They are especially seen in living beings, and most especially in human beings.

questions.question: What effect does life have on a person’s relation to the universe?
questions.answer: It gives the person a wide capacity that ties him to the whole universe.

questions.question: What does the statement that He “does all things in all things” mean in simple words?
questions.answer: It means His action and care are present throughout creation, even within individual things.

questions.question: How does the passage combine care for the whole universe with care for each person?
questions.answer: It says both happen together: the whole stays ordered while each being receives individual attention.

questions.question: What is organized in every living member of each species?
questions.answer: Its tools and bodily means are arranged in a fitting and orderly way.

questions.question: How is man different from other creatures in this explanation?
questions.answer: Man is presented as a concentrated display of many different blessings.

questions.question: What does the seed represent in relation to the melon?
questions.answer: It represents the melon in a compact and concentrated form.

questions.question: What does the seed-and-melon example prove about authorship or making?
questions.answer: It proves that the same maker who forms the whole must form the concentrated part.

questions.question: What final conclusion does the passage draw from the tree, fruit, and seed comparison?
questions.answer: The One who creates even the smallest living being is also the Lord of the entire earth and cosmos.

questions.question: In the opening comparison, what is the relationship between unity and sunlight?
questions.answer: Sunlight serves as an example of one source reaching many recipients.

questions.question: Why do reflections in drops of water matter in the argument?
questions.answer: They show that even very small things can display signs of the same single source.

questions.question: What idea is conveyed by saying the sun is at the mirrorlike heart of things?
questions.answer: Its reflected presence can be seen very near in many places at once.

questions.question: What does the passage say the wide reach of mercy proves first?
questions.answer: It proves the unity of the Merciful One.

questions.question: What second truth does that same mercy prove?
questions.answer: It proves that He has no partner.

questions.question: What two groups are highlighted when speaking about where Divine manifestations are found?
questions.answer: All living beings are mentioned, and human beings are given special emphasis.

questions.question: How does life make a creature comprehensive, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It gives it a broad range of relations and concerns beyond itself.

questions.question: How does mercy display glory across the cosmos and the earth?
questions.answer: It does so by appearing in a unified and all-inclusive way everywhere.

questions.question: What is gathered in each individual living member of a species?
questions.answer: Samples of the many bounties given by Allah are gathered in each one.

questions.question: What important balance is described in the care of individuals?
questions.answer: Each individual receives special care without damaging the order of the whole.

questions.question: Why is man called a concentrated form of bounty?
questions.answer: Because many kinds of blessings are brought together in him in a focused way.

questions.question: In the melon example, what is needed to draw out and shape the seed properly?
questions.answer: Precise knowledge and wise law are needed.

questions.question: How does that example support the larger argument about creation?
questions.answer: It shows that the maker of a small, concentrated part must be the maker of the larger whole it comes from.

questions.question: If the cosmos is like a tree and man is like a seed, what does that say about the Creator?
questions.answer: It says the Creator of man is also the Creator of the entire cosmos.

questions.question: What everyday natural example does the passage use to make an abstract belief easier to understand?
questions.answer: It uses the example of the sun and its reflections.

questions.question: How can a person know that many reflections do not mean many suns?
questions.answer: Because the same qualities appear across all the reflections, pointing back to one source.

questions.question: In that comparison, what does nearness mean?
questions.answer: It means the sun’s effects appear present in each reflecting object.

questions.question: What Divine quality in the passage is described as reaching all things like light?
questions.answer: Mercy is described that way.

questions.question: What belief is strengthened by seeing mercy spread through everything?
questions.answer: Belief that Allah is one and without any partner is strengthened.

questions.question: What is found in things under the covering of mercy besides material blessings?
questions.answer: Manifestations of many Divine Names and a sign of Divine presence are found there.

questions.question: Why are human beings given special attention in this section?
questions.answer: Because they show these meanings more fully and in a more gathered way.

questions.question: What does the passage say life causes an individual to do?
questions.answer: It causes the individual to face toward and be connected with the universe as a whole.

questions.question: How does this support the claim that Allah works everywhere?
questions.answer: It shows that the One who gives such life must be acting across all levels of creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens in every member of living species?
questions.answer: Blessings are gathered there and the needed tools are arranged there.

questions.question: What does “without shattering the wholeness of the universe” mean in simple language?
questions.answer: It means individual care does not disturb the overall order of creation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the melon and seed example?
questions.answer: It gives a simple picture of how a whole and its concentrated summary come from the same maker.

questions.question: Why is the seed described as impossible for another maker to produce?
questions.answer: Because it depends on detailed wisdom and design taken from the whole fruit.

questions.question: In the last sentence, what three-level comparison is made?
questions.answer: Universe to tree or garden, earth to fruit or melon, and man to seed.

questions.question: What major conclusion should a student draw from that three-level comparison?
questions.answer: The Lord who creates the smallest living being is the same Lord who creates everything.

questions.question: What is the function of the sun example in the first paragraph of the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a concrete image for understanding how unity and oneness can be recognized.

questions.question: What do transparent and shining things show when they reflect sunlight?
questions.answer: They show signs of the same single sun.

questions.question: What does a person conclude after noticing those reflections in many different places?
questions.answer: He concludes that the source is one, not many.

questions.question: How does the passage move from the sun example to its main theological point?
questions.answer: It applies the same pattern to Divine mercy reaching all things.

questions.question: What does the universal spread of mercy tell us about Allah?
questions.answer: It tells us that He is one and has no partner.

questions.question: According to the passage, what appears in all things and especially in living beings?
questions.answer: Manifestations of many Divine Names appear in them.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect life with comprehensiveness?
questions.answer: Because life gives a being broad relations that link it to many parts of existence.

questions.question: What does a human being’s wide relation to the universe indicate about the Creator?
questions.answer: It indicates that the Creator’s care and action extend through the whole universe.

questions.question: What is meant by saying Divine glory is shown in the whole cosmos through mercy?
questions.answer: Mercy reveals Divine greatness everywhere in a unified way.

questions.question: How are individuals treated within that universal mercy?
questions.answer: Each one receives gathered blessings and specially arranged means suited to it.

questions.question: What special statement is made about man?
questions.answer: Man is a concentrated place where many kinds of Divine bounty are made known.

questions.question: How does the melon-seed analogy help explain concentrated bounty in man?
questions.answer: Just as a seed contains a compact summary of the fruit, man contains a compact display of many blessings.

questions.question: What must the maker of the seed know how to do?
questions.answer: He must know how to derive it from the fruit with exact balance and wise design.

questions.question: What larger principle follows from that analogy?
questions.answer: The maker of a summarized part must be the maker of the larger whole.

questions.question: State the final conclusion of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The Creator of even the smallest living being is necessarily the Creator and Sustainer of the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What comparison opens the passage and sets up its argument?
questions.answer: The passage begins by comparing Divine unity to the way one sun is reflected in many places.

questions.question: Which qualities of the sun are mentioned as appearing in reflections?
questions.answer: Its brightness, warmth, and colors are mentioned.

questions.question: Why do these shared qualities matter for understanding the example?
questions.answer: They show that many reflections can come from one original source.

questions.question: In the passage, what corresponds to sunlight in the spiritual meaning?
questions.answer: The all-reaching mercy of the Merciful One corresponds to it.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is shown by mercy reaching all things?
questions.answer: It shows His unity and the impossibility of any partner beside Him.

questions.question: What additional evidence is given besides mercy’s wide reach?
questions.answer: The passage points to the appearance of many Divine Names and a special manifestation in created things.

questions.question: In which creatures is this especially noticeable?
questions.answer: It is especially noticeable in living beings, and most clearly in man.

questions.question: What does life do for an individual’s awareness or relation?
questions.answer: It gives the individual a broad relation to the rest of the universe.

questions.question: How does that relation become evidence for oneness?
questions.answer: It indicates that the One who grants life is active in all things, not limited to one corner of creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say is gathered into every member of animate species?
questions.answer: Examples of Divine gifts are gathered into every one.

questions.question: How are the bodily means of living beings described?
questions.answer: They are arranged and ordered appropriately for each being.

questions.question: What tension does the passage resolve between the whole and the individual?
questions.answer: It shows that personal care for each being can exist together with the complete order of the whole universe.

questions.question: Why is the seed a powerful example in this argument?
questions.answer: Because it is a small but complete summary of a much larger product.

questions.question: What does the impossibility mentioned in the seed example teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that a different maker cannot produce the summarized part apart from the maker of the whole.

questions.question: What is the final cause-and-effect conclusion drawn from the tree, fruit, and seed imagery?
questions.answer: Since creation works like an ordered whole with concentrated forms inside it, the Maker of the smallest living being must also be the Maker of all existence.
